stops.note: 'favour, thanks'; the three Graces, the goddesses of charm, were the Gratiae
via Old French grace, used above all for God's unearned favour; 'Your Grace' addressed English kings until Henry VIII's time, when 'Majesty' took over, and dukes and archbishops kept it

current_meaning: elegance of movement; courteous goodwill; God's favour; a prayer before a meal
